# BSDL

BSDL is a header-only Bidirectional Scattering Distribution Library. It
contains BSDF closures and support code originally developed in Open Shading
Language's `src/libbsdl`, packaged here as a standalone C++ project.

## Dependencies

- C++17 compiler
- Imath

The BSDL library target itself depends only on Imath. `Threads` is used only by
the build-time LUT generator. OSL and OpenImageIO are not BSDL dependencies.

## Build

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/install
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
cmake --install build
```

The build always builds and runs `BSDL_genluts` to generate the BSDF lookup
table headers. The generated headers are installed with the public headers.

## CMake Usage

Installed package:

```cmake
find_package(BSDL REQUIRED CONFIG)
target_link_libraries(my_renderer PRIVATE BSDL::BSDL)
```

Source tree:

```cmake
add_subdirectory(path/to/BSDL)
target_link_libraries(my_renderer PRIVATE BSDL::BSDL)
```

The exported target is `BSDL::BSDL`. The source tree also provides the
un-namespaced `BSDL` target for compatibility.

## Configuration

Include `<BSDL/config.h>` before any other BSDL header. By default, BSDL uses
`bsdl::BSDLDefaultConfig`, which provides a CPU implementation using standard
C++ math functions.

Integrators that need custom math functions, namespace settings, or device
annotations can define the configuration macros before including
`<BSDL/config.h>`:

```cpp
#define BSDL_INLINE inline
#define BSDL_INLINE_METHOD inline
#define BSDL_DECL
#define BSDL_UNROLL()

#include <BSDL/config.h>

struct MyBSDLConfig : public bsdl::BSDLDefaultConfig {
    struct Fast : public bsdl::BSDLDefaultConfig::Fast {
        static BSDL_INLINE_METHOD float cosf(float x);
        static BSDL_INLINE_METHOD float sinf(float x);
    };
};

#undef BSDL_CONFIG
#define BSDL_CONFIG MyBSDLConfig
```

`BSDL_CONFIG` must name a type that is visible at the point where BSDL headers
are included. The type can derive from `bsdl::BSDLDefaultConfig` and override
only the pieces needed by the integrator.

## Spectral Tables

BSDL includes built-in sRGB spectral support. Additional Jakob-Hanika spectral
tables can be generated by calling `add_bsdl_library()` directly with
`SPECTRAL_COLOR_SPACES`:

```cmake
include(path/to/BSDL/bsdl.cmake)
add_bsdl_library(MyBSDL SPECTRAL_COLOR_SPACES ACEScg)
target_link_libraries(my_renderer PRIVATE MyBSDL)
target_sources(my_renderer PRIVATE ${MyBSDL_LUTS_CPP})
```

This optional path generates `.cpp` files for the requested color spaces and
returns them through `<target>_LUTS_CPP`.
